source("R/helpers.R")
library(lterdatasampler)
library(kableExtra)
library(sf)
library(ggspatial)
data(pie_crab)

To learn about the functions of the tidyverse, we will explore a dataset from the Long Term Ecological Research program Network. This data describes the body size of fiddler crabs in salt marshes from Florida to Massachusetts during the summer of 2016. You can read more about this data here

Climate change has caused this species to expand its range northward in response to ocean warming. As a result, we can use this data to observe Bergmann’s Rule in action. Bergmann’s Rule predicts that organisms at higher latitudes (more north) will have larger body sizes.

Let’s start exploring the data using R and RStudio to see if the sampled fiddler crabs follow this prediction.

Exploring the Data

We will need to start by installing the packages needed for these evaluations. We can do that with the install.packages() function. This may take a while, but don’t worry, once you’ve installed the packages on your computer once, you won’t need to do it again.

install.packages(c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "lterdatasampler"))

Now that our packages are installed, we need to load them into our R session. We can do this using the library() function, as shown below. This only needs to be done once per session.

library(lterdatasampler)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

Now that we have the packages loaded, we can get at our data. Let’s call it crab_data.

TipSyntax Alert

The <- symbol assigns a value to a named object in R.
Syntax: name <- value (e.g., x <- 42)
If x doesn’t exist yet, a new object is created; it x does exist, its value is replaced.

data(pie_crab) # load the data
crab_data <- pie_crab # rename the data
crab_data <- pie_crab %>% 
  slice(round(seq(1, n(), length.out = 20))) %>% 
  mutate(row = row_number(), .before = 1) %>% 
  select(!name)

site_options_filt <- c("any", sort(unique(as.character(crab_data$site))))
size_options_filt <- seq(1, 25, 1)

choices_filt <- expand.grid(
  site = site_options_filt,
  size = size_options_filt, 
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

make_code_filter <- function(site, size){
  conditions <- c(
    if(site != "any") paste0('site == "', site, '"'),
    if(size > 0) paste0('size >= ', size)
  )
  if(length(conditions) == 0) return("crab_data")
  paste0("crab_data %>%\n filter(", paste(conditions, collapse = ", "), ")")
}

choices_filt$code <- mapply(make_code_filter, choices_filt$site, choices_filt$size,
                        USE.NAMES = FALSE)

results_filt <- lapply(choices_filt$code, function(code) eval(parse(text = code)))

choices_filt$before <- vapply(results_filt, function(r) {
  kept <- crab_data$row %in% r$row
  html_table(select(crab_data, -row), row_class = ifelse(kept, "kept", "dropped"))
}, character(1))

choices_filt$after <- vapply(results_filt, function(r) {
  html_table(select(r, -row))
}, character(1))

ojs_define(choices_filt = choices_filt,
           site_options_filt = site_options_filt,
           size_options_filt = size_options_filt)
viewof site_filt = Inputs.select(site_options_filt, {label: "Site"})
viewof min_size_filt = Inputs.range([d3.min(size_options_filt), d3.max(size_options_filt)], 
{label: "Minimum size", step: 1, value: d3.min(site_options_filt)})
rows_filt = transpose(choices_filt)
match_filt = rows_filt.find(d => d.site === site_filt && d.size === min_size_filt)
{
  const pre = document.createElement("pre");
  pre.className = "plot-code";
  const code = document.createElement("code");
  code.textContent = match_filt.code;
  pre.appendChild(code);
  return pre;
}
{
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.className = "side-by-side";
  wrap.innerHTML =
    "<div><p><b>Before</b></p>" + match_filt.before + "</div>" +
    "<div><p><b>After</b></p>" + match_filt.after + "</div>";
  return wrap;
}
